questions.question: Which of the following acts gave legislative councils the power to discuss the budget?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following acts gave legislative councils the power to discuss the budget?
questions.solution: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was significant for increasing the number of additional (non-official) members in the Central and provincial legislative councils while maintaining an official majority. It expanded the functions of these councils by allowing them to discuss the budget and address questions to the executive. Additionally, the Act provided for the nomination of some non-official members to the Central Legislative Council by the viceroy based on recommendations from provincial councils and the Bengal Chamber of Commerce, and to the Provincial Legislative Councils by the Governors based on recommendations from various local bodies and associations.

questions.question: Trend of metallic character is moving from left to right in the period of periodic table.
questions.questionHtml: Trend of metallic character is moving from left to right in the period of periodic table.
questions.solution:
Explanation:

  • Metallic character refers to how readily an atom loses an electron. Conversely, the non-metallic character is concerned with how readily an atom gains electrons.
  • As we move from left to right in a period, the atomic radius decreases due to which attraction between the nucleus and electrons increases. Due to this attraction, it is easier to gain electrons rather than lose them.

Therefore, the metallic character decreases as we move from left to right in a period.

questions.question: The Vice-President who assumes the office of the President in case of vacancy due to death holds it for a maximum period of:
questions.questionHtml: The Vice-President who assumes the office of the President in case of vacancy due to death holds it for a maximum period of:

options.text: Till the date when newly elected President assumes office
options.html: Till the date when newly elected President assumes office

questions.solution:
The Vice-President who assumes the office of the President in case of vacancy due to death holds it for Six months at most.

Key Points
  • The Vice President holds office for five years.
  • The Vice President can be re-elected any number of times.
  • However, the office may be terminated earlier by death, resignation, or removal.
  • The Constitution does not provide a mechanism of succession to the office of Vice President in the event of an extraordinary vacancy, apart from re-election.
  • However, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha can perform the Vice President's duties as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha in such an event.

However, when the President dies in office and Vice President takes over as President, he can continue serving as the President for a maximum of 6 months within which a new President shall be elected.

questions.question: "When.......was born, the earth sank two and a half hands." The above statement /Folk saying is related to which historical personality of Uttar Pradesh?

  • There are many versions of Ala, in which some 52 and 56 battles are described.

  • The popularity of Jagnik's folk poem "Alh-Khand" is nationwide.

questions.question: 'Ijara' revenue system was started during the reign of
questions.questionHtml: 'Ijara' revenue system was started during the reign of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jahandar Shah.

Key Points

  • Ijarah system was a revenue farming system introduced by Jahandar Shah.
  • When peasants lacked the means to cultivate their land or cultivation was impossible due to a calamity, the lands were farmed out on ijara to a third party known as revenue farmers.
  • It was forbidden for revenue officials or their families to take land on ijara.
  • It was anticipated that revenue farmers would not take more from peasants than the stipulated land revenue.
  • The revenue farmer paid nine-tenths of the total collection to the government and retained the remainder as collection charges.
  • Jahandar Shah was a Mughal Emperor who ruled for a brief period in 1712–1713.

Additional Information

  • Farrukhsiyar was the Mughal emperor from 1713 to 1719 after he murdered Jahandar Shah.
    • Farrukh Siyar Farman in 1717 was a grant-giving concession to the English East India company and allowed them tax-free monopoly trade especially in the Mughal subah of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
  • Muḥammad Shah was the thirteenth Mughal emperor, who reigned from 1719 to 1748.
    • He was the son of Khujista Akhtar, the fourth son of Bahadur Shah I.
    • He ascended the throne with the help of the Sayyid brothers at the young age of 17 and later got rid of them.
    • His pen name was Sada Rangila (Ever Joyous) and was often referred to as Muhammad Shah Rangila.
  • Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal Emperor.
    • He was deposed by the British and exiled to Burma (Rangoon) following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

questions.solution: Oxygen is a crucial element for sustaining human life and is found in the Earth's atmosphere, making up approximately 20%. questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as a Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in May 2025?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was appointed as a Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. Poonam Gupta.

Key Points

  • Dr. Poonam Gupta was appointed as a Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in May 2025.
  • She has extensive experience in economic policy formulation and previously held significant positions at the World Bank and NCAER (National Council of Applied Economic Research).
  • Dr. Gupta specializes in macroeconomics, international trade, and development economics, making her appointment pivotal for RBI's policy and research initiatives.
  • Her role as Deputy Governor includes overseeing monetary policy, financial stability, and economic research within the RBI.
  • Dr. Gupta's appointment reflects RBI's focus on strengthening its leadership with globally acclaimed economists.

Additional Information

  • Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
    • The RBI is India's central banking institution, established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act.
    • It is responsible for regulating the Indian monetary policy, issuing currency, and maintaining financial stability.
    • The RBI has four deputy governors, each overseeing key functions such as financial markets, banking regulation, and monetary policy.
  • Deputy Governor's Role
    • A Deputy Governor of RBI plays a crucial role in formulating policies related to banking regulation, financial inclusion, and economic research.
    • They are part of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), which decides India's monetary policy framework.
  • National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER)
    • NCAER is one of India’s premier economic policy research institutions, focusing on empirical research and data analysis.
    • It conducts studies on economic growth, infrastructure, and trade, contributing to policy-making processes.
  • World Bank
    • The World Bank is an international financial institution providing funding and expertise to developing countries for development projects.
    • Dr. Poonam Gupta previously contributed significantly to the World Bank's research on trade and development.

questions.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan. Reason (R): The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan.

Reason (R): The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946.

Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.html: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
options.html: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:
Assertion (A): The Muslim league first approved the Cabinet plan. But when the Muslim League found out that Congress had the majority in the Constituent Assembly, they rejected the plan. Hence, statement  A is true.

Reason (R):  The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946 on 26 October. Hence, statement R is correct.

Though assertion and reason are individually true but A is about the cabinet plan and R is about interim govt, hence, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question: Which regulatory body notified the “Determination of Cost of Production Regulations, 2025”?
questions.questionHtml: Which regulatory body notified the “Determination of Cost of Production Regulations, 2025”?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is ​CCI.

In News

  •  The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has notified the “Determination of Cost of Production Regulations, 2025”, replacing its 2009 framework.

Key Points

  • Issued by: Competition Commission of India (CCI).

  • Replaces: 2009 Cost Regulations.

  • Objective: Strengthen scrutiny of predatory pricing and deep discounting, especially in e-commerce and quick commerce.

  • Predatory Pricing: Sale below cost of production to eliminate competition – covered under Section 4 (Abuse of Dominance) of the Competition Act, 2002.

  • Key Features of 2025 Regulations:

    • Flexible, sector-agnostic approach.

    • Case-by-case assessments for platform-based and digital markets.

    • Benchmark cost = internal production cost, not market value.

    • Rejects market value due to subjectivity and external influence (like brand perception, subsidies).

    • Aligns with global best practices and modern economic theories.

  • Modernization Goal: Better fit for platform economies, cross-subsidies, and dynamic pricing models.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.text: When total utility is maximum, marginal utility is zero.
options.html: When total utility is maximum, marginal utility is zero.

options.text: When total utility is decreasing, marginal utility is negative.
options.html: When total utility is decreasing, marginal utility is negative.

options.text: When total utility is increasing, marginal utility is positive.
options.html: When total utility is increasing, marginal utility is positive.

options.text: When total utility is maximum, marginal and average utility is equal to each other.
options.html: When total utility is maximum, marginal and average utility is equal to each other.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.

Key Points

  • Total Utility is the sum of all utilities derived by a consumer from all units of commodity consumed by him.
    • It rises when more consumption is done.
    • It suffers from reduced returns.
  • Marginal utility is the addition to the total utility derived by consuming an extra or additional unit of the commodity.
    • It drops with an increase in total utility.
    • It reduces the consumption of each additional unit.
 Total utility Marginal utility
Decreasing Negative
 Maximum  Zero
Increasing Positive
  • Unlike marginal utility, average utility is always positive, as it is a ratio of two non-negative values.
  • So, the graph of average utility always remains above the X-axis.
  • When average utility attains maximum value, it is equal to marginal utility.
    • Like the marginal utility curve, the average utility curve is also downward sloping.​

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
questions.solution: The British Constitution inspired India's law-making process, contributing features like the parliamentary system, rule of law, legislative procedures, and single citizenship. The Indian Constitution also drew from other constitutions: the Government of India Act of 1935 influenced federal schemes and emergency provisions; the French motto inspired the preamble; the Canadian Constitution shaped the federal structure and distribution of powers; the Irish Constitution influenced the Directive Principles of State Policy; the Australian Constitution contributed to trade freedom; the U.S. Constitution inspired the Fundamental Rights; the German Constitution provided emergency powers; the South African Constitution informed legislative procedures; and the Japanese Constitution influenced law-making procedures.

questions.question: Who among the following coined the name oxygen for the element released by mercury oxide in 1779?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following coined the name oxygen for the element released by mercury oxide in 1779?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Antoine Lavoisier.

Key Points

  • Antoine Lavoisier is known as the "Father of Modern Chemistry".
  • He coined the term "oxygen" in 1779 after conducting experiments with mercury oxide.
  • Lavoisier demonstrated that oxygen is a key component in combustion and respiration.
  • He also named hydrogen and helped reform chemical nomenclature.
  • Lavoisier's work laid the foundation for the law of conservation of mass.

Additional Information

  • Mercury Oxide Experiment:
    • Lavoisier heated mercury oxide and observed the release of a gas, which he identified as oxygen.
    • This experiment debunked the phlogiston theory, which was the prevailing theory of combustion at the time.
  • Law of Conservation of Mass:
    • Lavoisier established that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
    • This principle is fundamental to modern chemical equations and stoichiometry.
  • Chemical Nomenclature:
    • Lavoisier collaborated with other chemists to create a systematic method for naming chemical substances.
    • This new nomenclature helped standardize chemical language and improve communication among scientists.
  • Lavoisier's Publications:
    • His notable works include "Traité Élémentaire de Chimie" (Elementary Treatise of Chemistry) published in 1789.
    • This book is considered one of the first comprehensive chemistry textbooks and outlines the principles of the new chemistry.

questions.question: Government audit also includes the audit of government companies conducted by:
questions.questionHtml: Government audit also includes the audit of government companies conducted by:

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.html: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

Key Points

  • Government audit also includes the audit of government companies conducted by Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
    • The Comptroller and Auditor General is authorised to audit all receipts (both revenue and capital) of the Government of India and of Governments of each State and of each Union Territory having a legislative assembly.
    • The accounts of the Government Companies (including Companies deemed to be Government Companies as per the provision of the Companies Act) are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) under the provisions of Section 619 of the Companies Act 1956 and Section 139 and 143 of the Companies Act 2013.

Important Points

  • Article 148 of the Indian Constitution
    • ​There shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India who shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal and shall only be removed from office in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
  • Sh. K. Sanjay Murthy is the CAG of India.
  • Article 149 of the Indian Constitution
    • ​It includes Duties and Powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
    • The Comptroller and Auditor-General shall perform such duties and exercise such powers in relation to the accounts of the Union and of the States and of any other authority or body as may be prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament.
  • Role of CAG
    • It upholds the constitution of India and the laws of the parliament in the field of financial administration.
    • He advises the President with regard to the prescription of the form in which the accounts of the Centre and States shall be kept.
    • He submits his audit reports relating to the accounts of the Centre to the President, who shall, in turn, place them before both the houses of Parliament.
    • He submits his audit reports relating to the accounts of a State to the Governor, who shall, in turn, place them before the state legislature.
    • He acts as a guide, friend, and philosopher of the Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament.
